rationale:
Evidence from the development race (entityR2A): the oval finishes 60% of the time, but the s-bend and slalom both end off track (progress 0.33 and 0.17, every trial). Those failures happen early, before the robot covers much of the course, so the steering is too slow or too weak to hold the tape through sharp direction changes. The slalom's near-constant score of about 70 suggests a consistent, early loss of the line rather than random noise.

Changes: (1) kp 2.0 -> 4.0, so each sensor-signal unit produces twice the wheel correction and the robot reacts faster to offsets on bends. (2) kd 0.3 -> 1.0, to damp the extra proportional action and limit overshoot and oscillation on the quick alternations of the slalom. (3) base_speed 1.2 -> 1.0, so the robot has more time to correct at bend entry. The oval took 1.96 s at 1.2, so 1.0 should still finish near 2.3 to 2.5 s, which is under the 3 s limit. (4) Sensor x spacing widened from +/-0.03 m to +/-0.04 m (0.02 m spacing), so the outer sensors see the tape earlier as the robot drifts and give a larger, earlier signal. ki stays 0 to avoid integral windup on bends. Line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with progress rising well above 0.33 and 0.17. The oval should still finish, with a shorter time than before if the lower speed does not slow it too much. Hypotheses to check next: (1) if steering_oscillation rises sharply with kp 4 and kd 1, kp is too high and should come down toward 3. (2) If the s-bend still leaves the track at similar progress, the robot is too fast at bend entry and base_speed should drop to about 0.8. (3) If the oval no longer finishes, base_speed is too low or the robot is overcorrecting. Measurements requested: all metrics, so progress, rms_error and line_loss_events can be compared per track against the score formula.
